newsitem.title: USA: Golf Centers, Knightsbridge IPOs get strong start.
newsitem.headline: Golf Centers, Knightsbridge IPOs get strong start.

text.p: Demand for initial public offerings was strong on Friday with Wall Street driving up three companies including an oil tanker, a golf course real estate firm and a maker of telecommunications components.
Knightsbridge Tankers Ltd shares rose more than eight percent in heavy trading on their first day of trading, up rose 1-3/4 to 21-3/4 from their IPO price of $20.

The Bermuda company said it will use proceeds to buy five very large crude carrier oil tankers (VLCCs), hence the company's Nasdaq stock symbol, "VLCCF.O". Knightsbridge is a subsidiary of ICB Shipping BF of Sweden.
Golf Trust of America Inc shares rose 2-3/8 on the American Stock Exchange from their IPO price of $21, the top of its estimated pricing range of $19 to $21 a share.

The Charleston, South Carolina company buys golf courses and leases them to independent operaters. It will initially own 10 courses, including nine daily fee courses and one private country club course. Robertson Stephens & Co was the lead underwriter of the offering.

Ciena Corp had the strongest IPO on Friday, jumping 50 percent. Shares rose 11-1/2 to 34-1/2 as investors fought to get a piece of the company, which makes a system aimed at boosting the capacity of fiber optics systems.
Goldman Sachs was the lead underwriter of the IPOs of Ciena and Knightsbridge.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts on Friday:

-- Puro Water Group Inc shares rose to 6-5/8 after the 1.35 million share offering. Shares priced at $6 each, the middle of the estimated pricing range of $5.50 to $6.50. Laidlaw Equities was the lead underwriter of the IPO.
-- Specialty Care Network Inc shares rose to 1/4 from their IPO price of $8 each. Credit Suisse First Boston was the lead underwriter of the offering.

-- Four Media Co shares were flat at $10 a share after their market debut. The company provides technical, creative and broadcast services to owners, producers and distributors of television programming.
Both the estimated price range and the number of shares to be offered in the initial public offering were cut ahead of the IPO.
